data.title: CrimeNER: Curated Dataset and Methods for Research and Investigation in Language Intelligence
data.description: arXiv:2603.02150v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The extraction of critical information from crime-related documents is a crucial task for law enforcement agencies. The extraction of this information can be interpreted as a Named-Entity Recognition (NER) task. However, there is a considerable lack of adequately annotated data on general real-world crime scenarios. To address this issue, we present CrimeNER, a case study of crime-related NER, and a general crime-related Named-Entity Recognition database (CrimeNER-db), consisting of more than 1.5K annotated documents extracted from public reports of terrorist attacks and the US Department of Justice's press notes. We define 4 coarse types of crime entity and 21 fine-grained entity types. We address the quality of the presented database with fully supervised experiments using flat and nested NER architectures and zero- and few-shot experiments using Large Language Models (LLMs). The database is available on GitHub.
data.author: Miguel Lopez-Duran, Julian Fierrez, Aythami Morales, Ruben Tolosana, Daniel DeAlcala, Gonzalo Mancera, Javier Irigoyen, Oscar Delgado, Francisco Jurado, Alvaro Ortigosa
